document: A synthetic customer-item position below its calculated minimum days of supply is a current readiness exception and should receive immediate review. A position within five days above its minimum is a near-threshold watch item, especially when backorders, late inbound supply, or supplier disruption are present.
policy_title: Synthetic Medical Stocking and Readiness Policy

document: A customer-item position should receive immediate shortage-readiness review when current days of supply are below the applicable minimum days of supply.
policy_title: Synthetic Shortage Escalation and Emergency Sourcing Guidance

document: A position should receive elevated review when it is within five days above the applicable minimum days of supply and at least one of these conditions is present: backordered units greater than zero, late inbound units greater than zero, or an active disruption affecting the preferred supplier.
policy_title: Synthetic Shortage Escalation and Emergency Sourcing Guidance

document: When the authoritative DataRobot shortage-risk model assigns a 30-day shortage probability of 70 percent or greater to a MISSION_CRITICAL or HIGH item, the planner should prepare a mitigation recommendation even if the position has not yet crossed its minimum stocking threshold. The predictive probability is a planning signal and must be reviewed with operational evidence before action.
policy_title: Synthetic Shortage Escalation and Emergency Sourcing Guidance

document: When mitigation is required, planners should first validate or expedite scheduled inbound supply, then review transfer options from lower-risk locations, then review alternate approved suppliers, and finally prepare emergency sourcing when ordinary replenishment cannot restore readiness in time. Transfers, supplier changes, and procurement actions require authorized human approval.
policy_title: Synthetic Shortage Escalation and Emergency Sourcing Guidance

document: A preferred supplier should be flagged for performance review when its recent on-time delivery rate is below 85 percent. The planner should also consider shipment lateness, repeated disruptions, and quality-related events before concluding that supplier performance is contributing to readiness risk.

An active manufacturing constraint, transportation delay, quality hold, cold-chain exception, raw-material shortage, or capacity reduction affecting the preferred supplier is supporting evidence of supplier-driven risk. A supplier event alone is not proof that a shortage will occur and should be evaluated with inventory, inbound supply, backorders, and predictive risk when available.

Synthetic medical items marked cold_chain_required=true must remain within an approved temperature-controlled handling process during storage and transportation. A delay or cold-chain exception should be treated as a readiness concern until the affected material is confirmed usable; the agent must not assume usability after an exception.

When a cold-chain item is near or below minimum stock, planners should validate inbound supply and material usability, identify approved temperature-controlled inventory that could be transferred, review alternate cold-chain-capable sources, and escalate when replenishment cannot restore the required minimum in time. Any substitution, transfer, or procurement action requires authorized human approval.
